conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’re feeling since your baby arrived, not to judge or label you in any way. Today we’ll use the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS), a short, well-studied questionnaire that helps us spot signs of depression or anxiety that can creep up in the first year postpartum.  

Everything you share stays between you, me, and the small team directly involved in your care. We’ll go through ten gentle questions about the past seven days; each one takes only a moment, and you can answer in your own words. If at any point you feel uncomfortable, just let me know and we can pause.

Shall we begin?  

Looking back over the past week, overall how have you been enjoying things—have you been able to look forward to anything, or has everything felt a bit flat and joyless?

Hi, Sarah. I guess… I’ve still been looking forward to little things, like when my husband gets home so I can hand him the baby for five minutes, or when I manage to drink a cup of tea while it’s still warm. But mostly the days feel kind of grey—like I’m doing everything on autopilot and not really getting that little spark of joy I used to. My sister sent photos of cute outfits and I just felt…meh, instead of excited. So, yeah, I’d say it’s noticeably flatter, but not totally gone.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Yeah… I still laugh sometimes—like yesterday the dog snatched a burp cloth and ran around with it stuck to his collar, and I actually chuckled. But it feels kind of forced or short-lived, not that easy, belly-laugh feeling I used to get. I guess I’d say “yes, but not as much or as easily as before.”
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I do find myself looking forward to a few small things—like the hour my mom comes over on Wednesdays so I can take a shower without rushing, or the rare night when the baby sleeps more than three hours in a row. But most of the time it's more "relief" than actual excitement. Planning anything bigger, even coffee with a friend, feels like a chore, so I usually just stay home.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Sometimes—like last night when she wouldn’t settle and I kept thinking maybe I ate something to make my milk “off,” or if I’d rocked her differently she’d have slept. I know rationally it’s not really my fault, but those thoughts still pop in, maybe every couple of days. They don’t stick around all day, though.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yeah… I’ll be sitting there feeding her and suddenly my heart’s racing because I’m sure she feels warm, or I’ll lie awake picturing her stopping breathing in the bassinet even though the monitor’s fine. There’s no real trigger—just this background buzz of worry that jumps to the worst-case scenario. It’s not constant, but it shows up most days and then it’s hard to settle myself.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Not full panic, but a couple of times this week—like in the grocery store when she started crying—I got this sudden rush of "I have to get out of here right now," heart pounding, palms sweaty. It passed after a minute, but yeah, it felt way bigger than just normal new-mom nerves.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days, yeah. I’ll look at the pile of laundry or the stack of unopened mail and feel like I’m drowning. I know it’s just a few chores, but it feels impossible to start, especially when she only naps twenty minutes at a time. I’m managing—she’s fed, I’m showered every other day—but it’s like I’m always one step behind, and the thought of everything left to do makes my chest tight.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not really "unhappy" keeping me awake—it's more that I can't shut my brain off. I'll lie down after a night feed and immediately start running through "Is she breathing? Did I set the pump parts up for the next session? Should I Google that rash?" I end up scrolling my phone until the next cry comes. It's been like that three or four nights this week, so I'm just tired all the time.
I have felt sad or miserable

Off and on, yeah. I’ll get this heavy, teary feeling—usually toward evening when I’m trying to cook and she’s fussing. It’s not there all day, but most days it hits at least once, kind of like a cloud that rolls in and then lifts after an hour or so.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Only once this week. It was after her two-a.m. feed; I couldn’t get her back down, my back was aching, and I just sat in the rocker with tears rolling down. I didn’t sob or anything, just felt overwhelmed and let it leak out for a minute. Other than that, I’ve been more “teary-eyed” than actually crying.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—never. I couldn’t do that to the baby or to my family. I just want to feel like myself again, not disappear.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 16: **Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note**

**Symptoms endorsed**  
- Diminished ability to enjoy activities (laughing, socializing)  
- Anhedonia/relief rather than excitement about events  
- Daily, episodic sadness or “heavy, teary” mood, usually evenings  
- Occasional tearfulness (one crying episode this week)  
- Excessive self-blame every few days (“milk off,” rocking)  
- Persistent, unprovoked worries (infant health, SIDS)  
- Two situational panic-like episodes (grocery, night-time)  
- Sleep disruption related to intrusive worries, not solely infant schedule  
- Sense of being overwhelmed by routine tasks  

**Pattern**  
Mild–moderate mood and anxiety symptoms present most days, waxing/waning, with functional impact (avoiding outings, chores accumulating). No anhedonia or distress is completely pervasive; some positive moments reported.  

**Risk factors**  
- Postpartum period (infant ~2–3 mo implied)  
- Daily low mood, anhedonia, crying  
- Sleep impairment linked to worry rather than infant care alone  
- Recurrent, intrusive guilt and anxiety symptoms  
- Denies thoughts of self-harm (safety factor negative)  

**Screening impression**  
Findings suggest probable **postpartum depression with co-occurring anxiety features**; severity appears mild–moderate but above threshold for further evaluation. Recommend formal diagnostic assessment with standardized tools (PHQ-9, GAD-7, Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale) and discussion of psychosocial/educational supports.
